signature.name: Shaniwar Wada
signature.detail: The fortified palace of the Peshwas is Pune's defining monument, famous for its massive gates and the stories tied to its ruins. Go early morning to avoid the heat and crowds, and note the entry ticket is small but paid.

signature.name: Aga Khan Palace
signature.detail: A grand palace with serene gardens, best known as the place where Mahatma Gandhi was interned. It is a peaceful, must-see stop; visit in the cooler morning hours and allow an hour or two.

signature.name: Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati Temple
signature.detail: One of Pune's most beloved and visited temples, dedicated to Lord Ganesha and especially vibrant during festivals. Dress modestly, remove shoes, and expect queues; early morning is calmest.

signature.name: Sinhagad Fort
signature.detail: A hill fort with sweeping views and a strong place in Maratha history, popular for a half-day trip from the city. Go early to beat the heat and traffic, and wear shoes with grip for the uneven paths.

signature.name: Pataleshwar Cave Temple
signature.detail: A rock-cut cave temple carved from basalt, right in the middle of the city and a quiet contrast to the busy streets. It is quick to see; combine it with nearby central sights and visit in daylight hours.
